title: Deadlock with .Result
cards/0/body:
The UI thread calls GetDataAsync().Result and blocks. Inside GetDataAsync, the continuation after await wants to return to the UI thread. But that thread is blocked, waiting for this very task.

Each waits for the other: a deadlock.
cards/1/task: Switch the handler to .Result and drive the program into a hang.
cards/2/q: What is the UI thread waiting for?
cards/2/options/0: For the GetDataAsync task to complete
cards/2/explain: .Result blocks the thread until the task completes.
cards/3/q: And what is the task waiting for?
cards/3/options/0: For the UI thread to run its continuation
cards/3/explain: The reply has already arrived. All the task needs is to run its continuation, which sits in the blocked thread's queue.
cards/4/task: Keep .Result, but move the code to a console app. Will it hang?
cards/5/q: Why doesn't .Result hang in a console app?
cards/5/options/0: There's no context: a pool thread runs the continuation, and it's free
cards/5/explain: Without a context, the continuation doesn't need the blocked thread.
cards/6/body:
In a console app or ASP.NET Core, .Result won't hang, but the thread still sits idle. Under load that's pool starvation (lesson 5).

Blocking on async code is bad everywhere.
cards/7/items/0: The UI thread calls GetDataAsync().Result and blocks
cards/7/items/1: The request goes out to the network
cards/7/items/2: The reply arrives and the continuation is queued to the UI thread
cards/7/items/3: The UI thread can't run it: it's waiting for the task
cards/7/items/4: Nobody ever gets what they're waiting for
cards/7/explain: The wait cycle: thread → task → thread.
cards/8/q: Where can this deadlock happen? Select all that apply.
cards/8/explain: It takes a single-threaded context. Old ASP.NET had one (AspNetSynchronizationContext); ASP.NET Core doesn't.
